rv.q: “Sunset Boulevard,” which opened Sunday night at the St. James Theatre, is Broadway’s most exhilarating show in years.
The revival opening tonight at Broadway‘s St. James Theatre is a stunner, stark always, funny sometimes and ultimately terrifying.
Director Jamie Lloyd’s revival of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s musical traps us in a relentless state of frisson for its two and a half hours.
Scherzinger has plainly been waiting for the right stage, and she puts every bit of fierceness and charisma into proving herself.

None of Lloyd’s hipster ideas to make extensive use of live video feeds and have his charming and judiciously understated male lead, Tom Francis, start the top of Act 2 while walking down 44th Street and singing live among the tourists into a camera would have worked without a Norma who could deliver Lloyd Webber’s best score.
Theater and film converge to brilliant effect at the start of Act II, when Joe throws open a door and steps out onto 44th Street.
Better to give yourself over to the tempest than to ask too many questions.
Not physically, not dramatically and certainly not vocally.
Part of what makes this revival so absorbing is that you don’t always know where to look—at the actor on stage or the same actor live on screen.
Effectively, this is a "Sunset Boulevard" for the sensation generation.
As Norma and as herself, Scherzinger ignites multiple blazes of originality, mischief, wit and drama in the stupendous revival of the classic Andrew Lloyd Webber musical.

In doing so, Lloyd has somehow managed to create a giddily thrilling revival, with star Nicole Scherzinger delivering one of the greatest performances I’ve ever seen as a psychotic Norma Desmond for the TikTok era.
The answer is a resounding yes.

If there's one reason why you should go to see Sunset Boulevard, the radical revival now playing on Broadway it's this: to see how far the contemporary theatre dares to go in reinterpreting a classic.

And these two stars do, to quote the script, have faces. And voices. And presence. A singer of phenomenal power and range, Scherzinger hits and holds the notes written by Andrew Lloyd Webber in a way that can induce gasps (not to mention two mid-show standing ovations at my performance).
On the whole, it makes for exciting, fascinating theater.
Mr. Lloyd’s “Sunset Boulevard” shines most brightly when this humanity blazes through the undeniable theatrical dynamite he summons throughout.
Lloyd's Sunset Boulevard pulls you into a theatrical universe all its own.
But more often than not, it just feels like sleepwalking.
The results are decidedly mixed mostly due to a failure to settle on a tone plus some head-scratching additions that have nothing to do with the story.
Evaluating it as a production of Sunset Boulevard seems beside the point, since Lloyd only seems concerned with the material insofar as he can put his own stamp on it.
The result—which gloriously stars Nicole Scherzinger as fading silent-screen idol Norma Desmond—is unique.
This Sunset Blvd....favors innovative staging over emotional involvement.

But take away everything except the words and the music here and you’ve exposed how tedious a musical Sunset Boulevard really is, even with a scintillating presence like Nicole Scherzinger at the center.
Putting a video camera(s) on stage and having live actors taped so that their faces can be magnified on big screens has become the most tiresome directorial crutch of this century.
It's a relentless and exhausting way to treat an audience.
But my attention shifted during a telling moment involving Tom Francis as Joe Gillis, the failed young Hollywood screenwriter.
The frightening reality of our closeness to her in Jamie Lloyd’s imaging is a journey worth taking.
The overall effect of Lloyd’s Sunset Boulevard is a very Hollywood one — a remake that’s so focused on flashy surfaces and fan service that it loses a bit of its heart and soul along the way.
...is a stark reminder of what happens when humankind refuses to accept mortality
Enjoy it for what it is….. it really is quite good if you let it.
Overall, “Sunset Boulevard” is a riveting and scorching new Broadway production.
Sunset Boulevard is the best show of the Broadway season, a powerhouse that should (and will) be remembered come Tony time.

cn.t: Lloyd's radical, stripped-down revival earns acclaim for Scherzinger's transcendent performance and bold cinematic staging, though some critics find the over-the-top direction relentless and the concept overshadows the material.

vr.q: one of the best things that I saw, not just this year, but maybe in my entire life
Nicole, who was giving the performance of a literal lifetime. She's not afraid to be funny and goofy and over the top. She is the perfect Norman Desmond.
I think this is a pretty Sensational night at the theater and it has to be a five-star verdict
this is Jamie Lloyd at his absolute best, and the phenomenal central performance by Nicole Scherzinger makes this an absolute must see
Simply put, this is an unforgettable, must-see production and could easily be THE theatrical event of the season.
I say go see the show because it is Wackadoo crazy in the most entertaining way and Nicole scherzinger's performance is equally melodramatic camp and her vocals are amazing
I loved Jamie Lloyd's direction but here's the thing at least half of what it takes to put on a good revival is choice of material and for that reason I can't comfortably call this a good revival
